- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days, then underestimates later.
- Forecasts tend to peak too early after sharp spikes in history (e.g., 51.08 → 50.44), then drop too aggressively.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion in the 10–20 day window; true values often revert to higher historical levels after initial spikes.
- Forecast bias is stronger in the 15–30 day horizon; model underestimates true values in this range, especially when true values are above 50.
- Model shows persistent lag in responding to recent high values; true values often rise faster than forecasted.
- Overshoot correction: if forecast exceeds true value by >5% in first 3 days, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Horizon-specific: for 30-day forecasts, model underestimates true values by 2–4% in the last 10 days; apply upward bias of 2–3% to compensate.
- Avoid overfitting to recent spikes; if history includes a spike >50, forecast should not peak above 52 unless confirmed by 2+ consecutive days of higher values.
